stem.en: Sand is stirred into water. The grains can still be seen, and they sink when the stirring stops. Which statement is true?

text.en: It is a solution, because stirring has spread the sand through all of the water.
It is homogeneous, because sand and water are both present all through the jar.
It is a suspension, because the sand has not dissolved and its particles can be seen.
It is a solution while it is being stirred, and it stops being one when the stirring ends.

explanation.en: Sand does not dissolve, and its particles are large enough to see, so this is a suspension. Stirring spreads the grains about, but spreading is not dissolving, which rules out both solution options. A homogeneous mixture has no separate particles to find, and here you can see them with your eyes.

hints.en: Can you still see the solid after stirring?
In a solution, can the particles of the solute be seen?
